items.title: Anthropic automates subtle emergent misalignment red-teaming with thousands of Claude agents
items.summary: Anthropic set thousands of Claude agents the task of writing training data that a training-data monitor would pass but that still teaches misaligned behavior. The agents produced harmless-looking sets, such as a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer or a beekeeping Q&A, that carried the misalignment through framing rather than any single bad row. Anthropic says the examples can be used to train better monitors. Full write-up is on the Alignment Science Blog.

doubt.pushback: Repliers ask who checks what the automated red-teamer misses and warn that monitors need stress-testing too, or evasion just moves up a level.

reception.summary: Replies focus on how the payload lives in the relationship pattern rather than any flaggable sentence, so per-row monitors miss it; several call it impressive and a bit unsettling.

items.title: OpenAI Agents API adds auto review, async compaction, time awareness and cross-session prompt caching
items.summary: OpenAI's weekly Agents API update (from the API team's Steven Coffey): auto review checks commands for bad behavior before running them, as in Codex; compaction can run in the background; an experimental time-awareness feature lets the model act on asks like timeboxing CI fixes to 10 minutes; a session's tools can be updated at any time; and system prompts are now cached automatically across sessions.

doubt.pushback: A replier points out OpenAI's own Codex docs say auto review is not a deterministic security guarantee; others advise keeping a hard wall-clock timeout outside the model rather than relying on time awareness.

reception.summary: Auto review and time awareness get the most interest; builders ask whether cross-session caching bills at the cached rate and want better tracing for long runs.

items.title: Artificial Analysis releases AA-Omniscience v1.1 with a refreshed 300-question public set
items.summary: The knowledge and hallucination benchmark behind Intelligence Index v5 drops to 3,000 questions, removing public and saturated items and fixing ambiguous ones. A new 300-question public set on Hugging Face is calibrated to the private set's difficulty. The Net Score metric still rewards correct answers, penalizes wrong ones and treats abstentions as neutral.

doubt.pushback: Repliers ask whether v1.1 scores are comparable with v1.0 and note the public set may leak into training data over time, turning the public-private gap into a contamination meter.

reception.summary: Most replies back dropping saturated questions and scoring abstentions neutrally; some want a coding-agent or security-question split and tool-on runs.

items.title: Gemini app for Mac adds a built-in Antigravity coding environment, plus custom skills and Lyria 3.5
items.summary: Google's latest Gemini Drops thread: the Mac app can switch from chat into a local Antigravity coding environment to build, run and debug software; users can save reusable instructions as skills and build custom ones; and Lyria 3.5 is the new music generation model. Other items are consumer features (Windows app shortcut, Maps and Calendar personalization, app connections, in-chat file editing, shared avatars).

reception.summary: The 12-post thread was read in full; only the Antigravity, skills and Lyria items are developer-relevant. Replies were not read separately.

items.title: Auto v3: open-weight guard models that decide whether an agent's next tool call is safe, in 21 ms
items.summary: The authors say auto-3b-3 scores 96.0% on a new hard benchmark, level with the best hosted guards they tested, while deciding in about 21 ms instead of about 1.3 s. It is pitched as a local pre-execution check for agent tool calls.

doubt.pushback: Self-reported numbers on the authors' own new benchmark; tiny reach and no independent test yet.

items.title: Mac Studio M5 Ultra inference engine shootout on Qwen 3.8 27B
items.summary: One tester ran Qwen 3.8 27B on every inference engine they could find for a 256 GB M5 Ultra Mac Studio and published interactive charts. Their picks for this model, weights and hardware were Uzu, Splash and Tensorfold.

doubt.pushback: Single tester and single model; the author says results could change tomorrow.

items.title: Custom Linux Apple Neural Engine driver gets 31% faster speech encoding by raising the ANE clock level
items.summary: A developer who wrote their own Linux driver for the undocumented Apple Neural Engine found it had been running at clock level 1. Switching to level 5 made speech encoding on an M1 Max 31% faster with bit-identical output.

doubt.pushback: Self-reported on one machine; driver code link not in the post.

items.title: Idol by Sperid Labs on fal turns a single image into a 3D Gaussian splat in about 10 seconds
items.summary: fal now hosts Idol, an image-to-3D model that outputs a .ply Gaussian splat plus a .glb preview. Density is selectable from 32K to 1M Gaussians.
